title: Coincidence/Relevance Lemma is used but never proved

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
The Substitution Lemma (solution.tex:418-439) begins "We use that the interpretation ⟦T⟧_ρ depends only on ρ↾FV(T)", and the Monotonicity Lemma application case, sub-branch x∉FV(Q), x∈FV(P) (solution.tex:365-366) silently concludes q=q′, i.e. ⟦Q⟧_ρ=⟦Q⟧_{ρ′} because ρ,ρ′ agree off x and x∉FV(Q). Proposition "step" (solution.tex:503) similarly relies on "restricting ρ to FV(N) is legitimate". All three are the Coincidence/Relevance Lemma:

  If ρ(y)=ρ′(y) for every y∈FV(M), then ⟦M⟧_ρ = ⟦M⟧_{ρ′}.

This lemma is load-bearing (the redex-drop routes through the Substitution Lemma, which depends on it) but is never stated or proved.

FIX: Add it before the Substitution Lemma; prove by a one-paragraph structural induction on M (variable: ρ(y)=ρ′(y); application: IH on both subterms; abstraction: IH at ρ[z:=a],ρ′[z:=a] for all a, since the 1+‖a‖ shift depends only on a). Alternatively derive it as a corollary of (M≤) used in both directions plus antisymmetry of ≤_σ (Lemma Basic(c)). Then cite explicitly at solution.tex:421, 365-366, 503.

Difficulty: easy/routine; low risk; purely completeness, but genuinely needed.
